clue.text: A ballad Henry composed he proclaims publicly in Scotland (12, two words)

definitions.note: a herald makes public proclamations; Albany is one of the Scottish heralds

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of 'A ballad Henry' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minstrel sets a ballad about King Henry to music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Albany Herald is one of the officers of arms of the Court of the Lord Lyon, Scotland's heraldic authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Heralds in the Lyon Court read out royal proclamations, and Albany is the title of one such Scottish officer.

clue.text: Once mixed in a girl's grip, just the thing for loyal toast? (9, two words)

definitions.text: just the thing for loyal toast?
definitions.note: a drinking glass is what the toast is drunk from

indicators.note: the mixing word goes in, held between the article and the girl
a girl's grip holds the word for mixing inside her

parts.note: a lass is a girl
meng is an obsolete word meaning to mix

explanation.surface: Someone mixing a drink in a girl's hand thinks it ideal for toasting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once mixed' points to an obsolete word for mix, not an anagram. 'Loyal' hints at the Jacobites, whose secret toasts to the exiled Stuarts were drunk from such engraved glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen glasses are eighteenth-century Jacobite wine glasses engraved with a hymn ending 'Amen', used for toasting the exiled Stuart king.

clue.text: Antimalarial drug, what's normally submerged in wallop

indicators.note: the submerged thing goes in the word for wallop

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or wallop
a ria is a drowned river valley, normally under the sea

explanation.surface: A drug against malaria is mixed into a pint of strong beer, wallop being British slang for ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallop' looks like the beer but is the verb 'lam', to beat; a ria is a long inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Lariam is a brand name for mefloquine, a tablet taken to prevent or treat malaria.

clue.text: Mix with water, no good put in waste

indicators.note: the abbreviation for no good is placed inside the word for waste

parts.note: to blue money is to squander or waste it

explanation.surface: Diluting something with water is no good and puts it to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue (or blow) money is old British slang for squandering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunging is the potter's process of stirring clay together with water to make a slip.

clue.text: Anon exercised about tax I'll be harsh on those who lapse

definitions.text: I'll be harsh on those who lapse
definitions.note: spoken in the first person by the answer, a person

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the tax and I
exercised means worked over, so the letters of anon are rearranged

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer, worked up about tax, vows to come down hard on defaulters.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of 'I'll' does double duty, as wordplay and as the speaker. Novatian was a third-century Roman antipope.
explanation.definitionFit: Novatian refused readmission to the church to Christians who had lapsed into pagan sacrifice under persecution.

clue.text: I'll go to sea no more, outer covering half gone, water running out of leak

definitions.text: I'll go to sea no more
definitions.note: the answer speaks in the first person as a retired ship

indicators.note: only the first half of the covering is left, the rest lost

parts.note: a hull is a ship's outer shell

indicators.note: the water flows away out of the word leak

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: An old ship complains that its hull is half gone and water is leaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half gone' leaves HU from HULL; EA, an old word for a river, leaves LEAK to give LK.
explanation.definitionFit: A hulk is the body of an old ship stripped down and moored, no longer seaworthy.

clue.text: R-Roman maybe missing a drug to treat ADD

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter A drops out of the nationality

parts.note: a Roman is an example of an Italian

explanation.surface: A stammering Roman, short of a dose, needs medicine for attention deficit disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'R-' gives R on its own. ADD is attention deficit disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritalin is the trade name of methylphenidate, a stimulant prescribed for attention deficit disorder.

clue.text: A thing flitting nocturnally as of old

indicators.note: flitting means darting about, so the letters of 'A thing' move around

explanation.definitionFit: Anight is an archaic adverb meaning by night, in the night-time.

clue.text: Stoic principle, little good in major conflict

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good goes inside the battle

G is the short form of good

explanation.definitionFit: In Stoic philosophy the logos is the rational principle ordering the universe.

clue.text: It's good for gout: see everyone pour oil freely round centre of pangs

the middle letter of the word pangs

explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of POUR OIL wraps N, the centre of pangs, to give OPURINOL after ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Allopurinol is a medicine that lowers uric acid in the blood, preventing attacks of gout.

clue.text: Tahitian wrap, trim with nothing underneath

clue.text: Where on Sabbath rules are relaxed in Peru/Venezuela

definitions.text: Where on Sabbath rules are relaxed

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across the two country names

clue.text: Turkish governor not quite sound

parts.note: a sound argument is valid

explanation.definitionFit: A vali was the governor of a vilayet, a province of the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Part of column I learn back to front

parts.note: to get something can mean to learn or understand it

clue.text: Professional killer in Japan infiltrating North America

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so these letters go within the abbreviation

parts.note: J is the international vehicle code for Japan

clue.text: Parent deity seen in eastern temple

parts.note: pa is father, a parent
a god is a deity

explanation.definitionFit: Pagod is an old form of pagoda, a tiered Buddhist or Hindu shrine in Asia.

clue.text: Cross set caused regrouping

clue.text: As jokesmith I must surrender to G & S in spat?

clue.text: What wearies stevedores, we hear, drying quicker?

clue.text: Prejudiced against the handicapped, bleak about lives

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleak' looks like an adjective for gloomy but is the fish.

clue.text: Cop I tackled about murder involving Christian sect

explanation.walkthrough: OPIC, the anagram of 'Cop I', goes about HIT.

clue.text: Barrel in first-class carriage, provider of bracing draughts?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests drinks from the barrel, but here it means currents of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An air bath exposes the naked body to fresh air for health, as a bath does with water.

clue.text: Quite a lot of our ancestors will have been found in these bars

clue.text: Hot state making one hesitate over decision

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Getting into a fever makes someone dither over a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot state' reads as a fever but splits into hot and state; haver is chiefly Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to dither or be undecided, hemming and hawing before choosing.

clue.text: Composer universal in what's offered to satisfy consumers

ado means fuss or trouble

clue.text: Sounder rootling near sties, loosing bonds
